title: The Mystery in the Net
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan/Shinichi, Ran, Sonoko, Agasa, Haibara, Detective Boys, Detective Yokomizo) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved (person/location/object), sharing an `order` integer so edges belonging to the same occurrence can be grouped without a reifying node. The old wiki-summary case file (cases/ep246-247_the_mystery_in_the_net.json) named the correct culprit (Noboru Shimojo) and victim (Giichi Aramaki), so label.murderer_id is unchanged, but it collapsed the whole backstory into one generic event node and missed: (1) that Aramaki is implied to have also murdered the sailor-witness who could have corroborated the sons' account of the boat collision (never confirmed on-screen, flagged as presumed/unconfirmed here); (2) that the murder weapon boat was the same boat Shimojo and Yoshizawa were seen handling on the beach earlier that afternoon, which is real physical opportunity evidence against both of them, not just Shimojo; (3) the actual trick was not 'net + rising tide' alone (explicitly proposed and refuted mid-episode) but 'net + the same boat, filled with seawater, used as a weight over a buried victim, that later floats free with the tide' -- letting the culprit have a remote alibi; (4) the real deductive clues were the impossible precision of Shimojo's stated time of death and his foreknowledge of the order of incoming calls, not the vague 'suspiciously precise time of death' the old file gestured at without explaining the mechanism. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: The victim's cell phone and the victim's own body carry matching scratch patterns from sea shells on the beach -- proves the 8:41 PM 'answered' call was caused by waves rolling the corpse against a shell and pressing the buttons, not by Aramaki or the culprit actually picking up. This removes the sons' apparent alibi (that someone had to be alive/present with the phone), since the killer never needed to be there when any call came in.

Normal time-of-death indicators (post-mortem lividity, rigor mortis, body temperature) were all destroyed by the waves continuously repositioning and chilling/warming the corpse, so the police could only bracket death to the 6:00-9:30 PM window Aramaki was last seen alive to found dead -- yet Shimojo confidently stated Aramaki died 'around 8:00,' a precision only the actual killer could know.

Shimojo assumed, without being shown the phone log, that Yoshizawa's call to Aramaki had come before his own first call at 7:47 PM (the real order: Yoshizawa 7:02 PM, then Shimojo 7:47/8:03/8:18 PM) -- he could only know that ordering because he personally heard Aramaki's phone ring at 7:02 PM while he was still at the beach setting up the net-and-boat trap.
